public_rationale: Google identified Gemini Enterprise as a substantial source of growth. Microsoft specifically said Copilot helped increase commercial revenue per user. These disclosures contradict the categorical denial that AI helps other product categories grow beyond the two labs' compute purchases. They do not establish that AI explains most corporate growth or earns an adequate return on investment.
limitations: The evidence consists of management disclosures, not independent causal experiments.
The companies do not provide a complete revenue bridge excluding both labs.
The conclusion does not separately settle Amazon's contribution.

from_speaker: AI is not the reason that these companies are growing
outside of the compute spend from Anthropic and OpenAI

our_interpretation: The companies are Google, Microsoft and Amazon.
The plain reading denies a material contribution from AI beyond the two labs' compute purchases. It does not merely say AI contributes less than other businesses.
Use April–June 2026, the latest completed quarterly reporting period before publication.
Sales of AI products to other customers count even when those products incorporate models supplied by the two labs.
This is a qualitative causal claim, not a claim about a specified revenue amount.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable evidence attributes the companies' growth to other businesses and the excluded compute purchases, while showing no material additional contribution from AI.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Product-specific evidence shows AI contributing materially to growth beyond the excluded compute purchases at one or more named companies.
